reference.notes:
I made the fix with a one-line change to `src/query.ts`. `parseQuery` now builds its result with `Object.create(null)` instead of `{}`. The file had no bodies throwing `not implemented`. Before this, `parseQuery` existed but returned an object that inherits from `Object.prototype`. The working tree also already had the doc comment about the null prototype.

That one change covers the whole spec:
- Keys like `toString` or `valueOf` no longer pick up an inherited value, so they're stored as ordinary keys. A repeated key collects only the values from the query.
- The existing check on the decoded key still drops `__proto__` and `constructor` exactly as before.
- Repeated-key values are still ordinary arrays.
- Each call returns a new object.

`getQuery` in `src/utils.ts` returns `parseQuery`'s result directly, so it now returns a null-prototype object too. The other places that call `parseQuery` copy its result into a new object, so they behave as before.

I ran the full suite with `npx vitest run`: all 15 files and 631 tests pass, including 44 in `test/ufo-query-null-proto.test.ts` and 115 in `test/hidden-ufo-query-null-proto/`. I didn't run a separate type check.
